sources.title: Coinbase Advanced Trade REST API

sources.selection_rationale: Establishes the public no-auth market-data baseline and the private endpoint authentication boundary.

sources.title: Coinbase API-key authentication
sources.credibility_signals: Published by Coinbase Developer Platform for Coinbase App API authentication.
sources.selection_rationale: Defines human portal issuance, key/JWT use, restrictions, secure storage, and enable, regenerate, or disable lifecycle controls.

sources.title: Coinbase authorization and permissions

sources.title: Coinbase Get API Key Permissions

sources.title: Coinbase App rate limiting

sources.title: Kraken API rate limits

sources.title: Kraken API-key security

sources.title: Apple Keychain Services
sources.credibility_signals: Apple Developer primary documentation for Security framework Keychain Services.
sources.selection_rationale: Defines the native encrypted storage and retrieval boundary for small provider secrets on Apple platforms.

sources.title: Apple updating and deleting keychain items
sources.credibility_signals: Apple Developer primary Security framework guidance.
sources.selection_rationale: Supplies native replacement and deletion operations needed for two-phase activation, rotation, and local revocation.

sources.title: Apple keychain-item accessibility
sources.credibility_signals: Apple Developer primary Security framework access-control guidance.
sources.selection_rationale: Defines device-lock, passcode, device-only, and user-presence tradeoffs for local secret activation.

sources.title: Windows Credentials Management
sources.credibility_signals: Microsoft Learn primary Win32 documentation for Credential Management APIs.
sources.selection_rationale: Establishes user-logon-session native credential storage and the Windows integration family.

sources.title: Windows CredWriteW and CredDeleteW API family
sources.credibility_signals: Microsoft Learn primary Win32 Credential Management API reference; the selected page links the same official API family.
sources.selection_rationale: Supplies native create or update semantics; companion CredDeleteW supplies deletion for rotation and local revocation.

sources.title: Windows CryptProtectData
sources.credibility_signals: Microsoft Learn primary Win32 Data Protection API reference.
sources.selection_rationale: Documents same-user and normally same-machine protection plus the broader LOCAL_MACHINE flag that must not become the per-user default.

sources.title: freedesktop Secret Service API 0.2 DRAFT
sources.credibility_signals: Primary specification published by freedesktop.org for desktop Secret Service implementations.
sources.freshness_signals: Version 0.2 DRAFT states publication date 2026-04-08; accessed 2026-07-22.
sources.selection_rationale: Defines Linux secret items, sessions, locks and prompts, create or replace and delete operations, and the rule that attributes are not secret.

sources.title: RFC 8252: OAuth 2.0 for Native Apps
sources.credibility_signals: RFC Editor publication of IETF consensus BCP 212.
sources.selection_rationale: Requires external-browser authorization and PKCE and defines native redirect patterns and public-client secret limitations.
sources.selection_note: Excluded duplicate of PAPER-001; the RFC is registered once under its original source ID.

sources.title: RFC 8628: OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant
sources.credibility_signals: RFC Editor publication of an IETF OAuth Working Group Proposed Standard.
sources.selection_rationale: Defines the device flow, mandatory human authorization, polling and slowdown rules, and metadata needed to prove provider support.
sources.selection_note: Excluded duplicate of PAPER-002; the RFC is registered once under its original source ID.

sources.title: RFC 9700: Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security
sources.credibility_signals: RFC Editor publication of IETF consensus BCP 240 updating core OAuth security guidance.
sources.selection_rationale: Provides current PKCE, grant selection, token replay, refresh-token rotation, and metadata requirements for any future provider OAuth flow.
sources.selection_note: Excluded duplicate of PAPER-006; the RFC is registered once under its original source ID.

sources.title: RFC 7009: OAuth 2.0 Token Revocation
sources.credibility_signals: RFC Editor publication of an IETF OAuth Working Group Proposed Standard.
sources.selection_rationale: Defines provider-supported HTTPS access- and refresh-token revocation semantics for lifecycle design.
sources.selection_note: Excluded duplicate of PAPER-007; the RFC is registered once under its original source ID.

sources.title: RFC 8414: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata
sources.credibility_signals: RFC Editor publication of an IETF OAuth Working Group Proposed Standard.
sources.selection_rationale: Defines capability discovery for endpoints, grants, scopes, registration, revocation, and introspection rather than relying on assumptions.
sources.selection_note: Excluded duplicate of PAPER-005; the RFC is registered once under its original source ID.

sources.title: RFC 7591: OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration Protocol
sources.credibility_signals: RFC Editor publication of an IETF OAuth Working Group Proposed Standard.
sources.selection_rationale: Defines automated client registration while making clear that provider-controlled initial credentials or software statements may still be prerequisites.
sources.selection_note: Excluded duplicate of PAPER-003; the RFC is registered once under its original source ID.
